chunks: Whoever provides for the breaking of the fast (iftar) of a fasting person, for him shall be the like of his reward.

key_terms.فَطَّرَ: to provide iftar (the meal breaking the fast at sunset)

ai.seo_question: What reward does a person receive for providing iftar to a fasting Muslim?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of vicarious merit in Islamic worship — that one who facilitates the religious observance of another receives a reward equivalent to that of the observer. The context is Ramadan, where providing iftar (the evening meal breaking the fast) to a fasting Muslim entitles the provider to a full share of the fasting reward, without diminishing the faster's own reward. This teaching encouraged the early Muslim community to support one another in worship, particularly the poor who could not easily maintain their fast.
